voiceover: You've read the argument. But could you explain it to a friend tomorrow, from memory? That's what a mastery track is for. The deep dive tells you what the argument is. This track makes you able to use it. Take the Kalam. It starts with the argument in brief: whatever begins to exist has a cause, and the universe began to exist. Then three earned levels. Bronze: rebuild it. Silver: defend it cold. Gold: handle an objection you've never seen, then prove it again weeks later. Understand it: not more prose, but the load-bearing structure, defended bone by bone, then proven from memory. Practice it, with flashcards and drills, including one that makes you rebuild the reply, word by word. Then prove it. Mastery isn't a feeling. Don't trust the warm glow of having read it. Prove it cold. Explain it back in your own words and get a score, then answer the objections without notes. Don't just read the case for your faith. Be able to give it. Find the mastery tracks in the Evidence Library at apologia daily dot com.
